o1.biggest_strength: A complete 4-week calendar with working titles for every later slot. The week 1 drafts use the customers' own phrases ('replaying emails', 'quit by day three', 'ten minutes is a fantasy') in our warm voice, and each ends with one small action.
o1.biggest_mistake: The success bar is set at the 143 installs-per-post baseline (about 3,440 total) when this mix should roughly double that, so the plan could fail badly and still count as a win. The pickup-in-the-car post also goes out at 20:30, long after pickup.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Project expected installs from the theme mix (about 6,580) and set the success bar near that, not at the old average.

o2.biggest_strength: The measurement is rigorous and every figure checks: a 6,580-install projection, 3.4% saves, 1.7% shares, a 3,390 four-week baseline, and a real 5,000-install target. It also batch-submits weeks 2 to 4 for review on 16 November as a safety net.
o2.biggest_mistake: Weeks 2 to 4 get only one angle line per week, not post-level ideas. It also keeps a weekly stress-at-work slot, a 95-install theme, when kindness or more sleep would likely earn more.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give working titles for all 18 posts in weeks 2 to 4 and swap the stress-at-work slot for sleep or kindness.

reason: Both make the right big call: sleep, narrator clips, evenings. Output 2 sets a success target I'd actually hold the team to, and its numbers check out, while Output 1's bar is so low it can't fail. Output 1's fuller calendar nearly closes the gap.
